body:
The exclusive claim, the name sanitizing and the idle cleanup hold up, but the runner-wide slot makes a repo's path depend on other repos' load, so it is not stable at capacity above 1. Two ways, by how stable the path should be, both as the default without an option:

1. Stable across sequential jobs, all OSes: claim the lowest free `workspaces/<owner>/<repo>/<n>` per repo instead of using the runner-wide slot. A repo with one job at a time always gets `/0`, concurrent jobs of the same repo get `/1`, `/2`, like GitHub runners sharing a host each get their own `_work`. This drops the dependency on https://gitea.com/orbit/orbit/pulls/1401 and covers parallel called-workflow jobs and runners sharing `host.workdir_parent` without the random fallback.
1. Stable across all runs, Linux: a job that finds `workspaces/<owner>/<repo>` in use runs its processes in a private mount namespace with its own directory bind-mounted there, so concurrent jobs share the path with separate contents. Steps start through a re-exec helper that unshares, bind-mounts and execs, as Go can't mount between fork and exec. The runner's own file I/O (action copies, `GITHUB_ENV`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`) uses the backing directory. It needs root or unprivileged user namespaces, which Ubuntu 24.04 restricts unless an AppArmor profile allows them for the runner. At job end, remove the contents but keep the directory, as removing a mountpoint detaches it in other namespaces. Without namespace support, fall back to the first way.

Caveats of the second way to document: in a namespaced job, `docker run -v "$PWD:/src"` against the host daemon mounts the other job's directory, and under user namespaces `sudo` fails. A repo's only running job keeps a plain host path, where both work.

Also:

1. Name the workspace dir after the repo instead of `hostexecutor`, matching GitHub's `_work/<repo>/<repo>`. Every host job's `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` ends in `hostexecutor` today, so concurrent `docker compose` projects of different repos collide on the default project name.
1. Either way, drop `host.stable_workdir` and its idle cleanup gating. As is, turning the option off leaves its dirs uncleaned.
1. List the host dir cleanup in the README's idle cleanup section.

_Written by Claude (Opus 5.5)._
I guess this could be `host.workdir_stability = all | sequential`, but needs more thought put into it. The `all` mode with namespaces is especially problematic and will only work on Linux.
